'''Saralees Nadarajah''' is a British statistician and researcher specialising in distribution theory, [[extreme value theory]], [[nonparametric statistics]], and their applications. He is also a professor at the [[Department of Mathematics, University of Manchester]] and has worked at the Department of Statistics at the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln|University of Nebraska-Lincoln]] and the [[University of South Florida]].

==Early life and education==
Nadarajah was born in [[Sri Lanka]] and grew up in [[Zimbabwe]].{{Citation needed|date=August 2023}} He obtained his B.Sc. in [[mathematics]] from the [[University of Zimbabwe]] in [[Harare]].{{Citation needed|date=August 2023}}
Nadarajah earned his M.Sc. and Ph.D. degrees in [[statistics]] from the [[University of Sheffield]] in the UK, in 1991 and 1994 respectively.<ref>https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37300433000</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=229494|title=Saralees Nadarajah |website=[[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]}}</ref>

==Career==
As of April 2025, Nadarajah is a [[professor (academic rank)|professor]] at the [[Department of Mathematics, University of Manchester]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.maths.manchester.ac.uk/about/people/academic-and-research-staff/ | title=Academic and research staff (A-Z) - Department of Mathematics - the University of Manchester }}</ref> He was previously affiliated with the Department of Statistics, [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]] and the [[University of South Florida]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dl.acm.org/do/10.1145/contrib-81320493026/abs/|title=Saralees Nadarajah - Home|website=Author DO Series|doi=<!-- none --> }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=Optimal design of mixed-effects PK/PD models based on differential equations|first1=Yi|last1=Wang|first2=Kent M.|last2=Eskridge|first3=Saralees|last3=Nadarajah|date=August 7, 2012|journal=Journal of Biopharmaceutical Statistics|volume=22|issue=1|pages=180–205|doi=10.1080/10543406.2010.513465|pmid=22204534|s2cid=42462863 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/statistical-science/volume-17/issue-2/A-conversation-with-Samuel-Kotz/10.1214/ss/1030550863.pdf | doi=10.1214/ss/1030550863 | title=A conversation with Samuel Kotz | date=2002 | last1=Nadarajah | first1=Saralees | journal=Statistical Science | volume=17 | issue=2 }}</ref>

Nadarajah is the founder of Educate Africa project which he started in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://imstat.org/2023/02/15/educate-africa-an-appeal-for-researchers/|title=Institute of Mathematical Statistics &#124; Educate Africa: an appeal for researchers}}</ref>

==Research==
Nadarajah specializes in statistical fields including extreme value and [[Distribution (number theory)|distribution theory]], [[nonparametric statistics]], [[information theory]], and reliability.<ref name="auto">https://minerva.it.manchester.ac.uk/~saralees/</ref><ref>{{Cite book |title=Extreme Events in Finance: A Handbook of Extreme Value Theory and Its Applications |last=Longin |first=Francois |publisher=[[Wiley (publisher)|Wiley]] |year=2016 |isbn=9781118650196 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=f1KzCgAAQBAJ}}</ref> His expertise also extends to [[sampling (statistics)|sampling theory]], statistical software development, and [[time series]] analysis.<ref name="auto"/> Nadarajah-Haghighi (UNH) class of distribution is named after him.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s13171-020-00203-6|title=Unit Nadarajah-Haghighi Generated Family of Distributions: Properties and Applications|first1=Suleman|last1=Nasiru|first2=Abdul Ghaniyyu|last2=Abubakari|first3=John|last3=Abonongo|date=August 1, 2022|journal=Sankhya A|volume=84|issue=2|pages=450–476|via=Springer Link|doi=10.1007/s13171-020-00203-6|s2cid=225695408 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>
